questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to sort your rubbish correctly at home
Why China produces so much of the world's plastic
How plastic is made from oil in big factories
Recycling problems and why reducing waste matters
questions.why: Neil asks if the recycling system is broken, and experts say reducing and reusing is better.

options: He forgot to put the recycling bins out
He missed his train
He was shopping for groceries
He overslept
questions.why: He says he'd forgotten to take the recycling bins out before the collection.

options: Britain stopped recycling paper and cardboard
Vietnam started accepting all of the world's waste
China stopped taking the world's plastic and paper
Plastic production fell for the first time in history
questions.why: Georgina says China used to accept 55% of the world's scrap, but in 2018 it stopped.

questions.q: Why are countries like Indonesia and Vietnam sending waste back?
options: They have no more space to store it in their ports
They say it's contaminated and harming nature
They want to be paid more money for taking it
They have built their own new recycling factories
questions.why: Neil says they argue it is contaminated and harming their own environments.

questions.q: What worries Professor Roland Geyer, despite greater public awareness?
options: People are now recycling far too much of their waste
Recycling workers are losing their jobs to machines
The public is not really interested in the problem
The virgin plastic industry is increasing production
questions.why: He says he sees no real action because the virgin plastic industry is increasing its production capacity.

questions.q: What surprising finding did Professor Monic Sun's experiments show?
options: People use more when they know they can recycle
People recycle much more when they feel guilty
Most people in the study don't recycle at all
Recycling makes people buy fewer new products
questions.why: She found that if people know recycling is an option, they tend to use more resources.

questions.q: According to Professor Sun, what is often not emphasised enough?
options: The many benefits of recycling for the planet
The number of recycling bins in each street
The labour and material costs of recycling
The high value of plastic scrap on world markets
questions.why: She says the cost of recycling isn't emphasised enough; there are significant labour and material costs.

questions.q: What does Professor Sun think our priority should be?
options: Recycling as much as possible
Reducing and reusing before recycling
Burning waste instead of burying it
Sending waste to other countries
questions.why: She says “reduce and reuse is better than recycling”.
